merger_description:
A consortium comprising investment funds advised and/or managed by affiliates of Stonepeak Partners LP (together with its affiliates, **Stonepeak**), and a fund managed by Axight Capital Limited (**Axight**), propose to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of Estia Health Holdings Ltd (**Estia**) (the **Acquisition**).

Stonepeak is a global alternative investment firm specialising in infrastructure and real assets. Stonepeak has an interest in Aura Holdings, a retirement village developer and operator in Queensland.

Estia is the ultimate holding company of the Estia corporate group, which operates residential aged care homes in Australia. Estia operates 94 homes nationally, with operations in Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia. Estia is currently majority owned by Bain Capital Private Equity.

Axight is an Abu Dhabi-based investment fund manager established by Lunate, an Abu Dhabi asset management firm. Axight operates as Lunate’s dedicated Asia-Pacific investment platform. Axight and Lunate do not hold any interests in any residential aged care business in Australia.

determination_table_content.details:
A consortium comprising investment funds advised and/or
managed by affiliates of Stonepeak Partners LP (together with its
affiliates, Stonepeak), and a fund managed by Axight Capital Limited
(Axight), propose to acquire 100% of the issued share capital of
Estia Health Holdings Ltd (Estia) (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

Stonepeak is a global alternative investment firm specialising in
infrastructure and real assets. Stonepeak has an interest in Aura
Holdings, a retirement village developer and operator in Queensland.
Estia is the ultimate holding company of the Estia corporate group,
which operates residential aged care homes in Australia. Estia
operates 94 homes nationally, with operations in Queensland, New
South Wales, Victoria and South Australia. Estia is currently majority
owned by Bain Capital Private Equity.
Axight is an Abu Dhabi-based investment fund manager established
by Lunate, an Abu Dhabi asset management firm. Axight operates as
Lunate’s dedicated Asia-Pacific investment platform. Axight and
Lunate do not hold any interests in any residential aged care
business in Australia

There is no overlap in Australia between Estia’s activities and the
activities of either Stonepeak and its connected entities, or Axight
and its connected entities.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The services provided by Aura Holdings (retirement villages), in
which Stonepeak has an interest and Estia (aged care) are
separate product markets.
• There are no relevant competitive overlaps between Estia and
either of Stonepeak or Axight (or their connected entities).

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
